page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of system memory. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this server features 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. The CPU allocation is dedicated, ensuring consistent access to compute resources. The processor includes a cache hierarchy consisting of 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the c2d-standard-8 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% of tested servers with a stress-ng single-core score of 2865.09. Multi-core CPU performance falls within the average range, scoring 11559.23 on stress-ng. Memory bandwidth benchmarks indicate average performance, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 553.27 GB/sec, while uncached large block read and write speeds measure 46.79 GB/sec and 32.75 GB/sec respectively. Other standard operations, such as gzip compression at 28.36 GB/sec and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression at 38.08 GB/sec, also align with average tier expectations. Geekbench testing yields average scores of 1658.0 for single-core and 6531.0 for multi-core workloads, including software compilation and ray tracing tasks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c2d-standard-8 offers a balanced resource density for workloads requiring dedicated AMD EPYC compute power without the overhead of local NVMe storage or GPU hardware. The 4 GB of memory per vCPU provides a standard ratio for compute-heavy applications that still require moderate memory capacity. This configuration is appropriate for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, text and image processing, and lightweight language model inference using small models.
